what_matters.head: Chip and AI stocks fell hard on Wednesday. US consumer prices rose more than expected in September, which raised bets on another Fed rate rise, and worries about how AI data centres are paid for spread.
what_matters.detail: Prices rose 3.7% from a year earlier, against the 3.6% analysts expected; excluding food and energy, 2.6% against 2.5%. Traders raised their bets on another Fed rate rise at the 28 Oct meeting, Stocktwits reported. Stocktwits also tied CoreWeave's fall to a Gartner forecast that over 80% of "neocloud" providers, the companies that rent out AI computing, will stop operating independently by 2030; Barron's tied it to CoreWeave's bonds, which traded at yields near 15%.

what_matters.head: Seoul's KOSPI fell 8% this morning and trading was halted for 20 minutes, its first circuit breaker in two and a half months. SK Hynix and Samsung led the fall.
what_matters.detail: Reuters tied it to Wall Street's tech sell-off after the US inflation data. Foreign investors sold a net 2.9 trillion won of shares. The index was heading for a seventh straight daily fall, its longest losing run since September 2024.

what_matters.head: TSMC's third-quarter revenue of US$46.72 billion beat the top of its own US$44.6–45.8 billion forecast. It forecasts US$52.3–54.3 billion for the fourth quarter.
what_matters.detail: Gross margin was 66.4%, inside its 65–67% forecast, and operating margin 58.7%, above its 56–58% forecast. For the fourth quarter it forecasts a 65–67% gross margin and a 56.5–58.5% operating margin. The call was still running when this was written, so any change to the capex plan is not covered. Not in Wednesday's US prices.

after_data.text: Anthropic told investors its third-quarter revenue was $16.8 billion, up from $11.6 billion in the second quarter, and that it was profitable on an adjusted basis, Reuters reported on Wednesday evening New York time, after the FT. Investor's Business Daily tied a fall in US tech futures to the news. Not in Wednesday's US prices.

In trading after Wednesday's close, CoreWeave fell another 5.9%, Nebius 3.9%, Bloom Energy 3.5%, Lumentum 3.1%, AMD 2.8%, Micron 2.7% and TSM 1.7% (last after-hours prices in the run). CoreWeave's chief executive told staff in a memo that 'there will be periods of time when the market misunderstands and acts irrationally', Bloomberg reported. Not in Wednesday's closing prices.

latest.tape_note: US stocks fell on Wednesday: the S&P 500 lost 1.1% and the Nasdaq 1.9%, while the Dow was little changed. Chip stocks fell 4.5% and are down 10.9% over five days. The 10-year Treasury yield rose after the inflation report, to 5.27% during the day, then ended slightly lower at 5.19%. The VIX rose 10% to 16.9. The US dollar index rose 0.4%. The US dollar also rose 0.4% against the Singapore dollar, twice its usual day; that window includes MAS's decision on Wednesday morning to leave its policy unchanged. Oil rose 1.0% and gold fell 1.7%.
latest.tonight: US producer prices for September at 20:30 SGT. The OCP Global Summit in San Jose ends today.

recent.headline: Chip and AI stocks fell hard on Wednesday. US consumer prices rose more than expected in September, which raised bets on another Fed rate rise, and worries about how AI data centres are paid for spread.
MAS left its Singapore-dollar policy unchanged this morning. All 10 analysts in a Reuters poll last week had expected it to tighten again, after a very slight tightening in July.

SK Hynix fell about 9% and Samsung about 8% by 13:05 Seoul time, after China's CXMT said it plans to launch a denser kind of server memory by the end of 2026. The Kospi was down 7.2% around midday, its lowest level since July.
SK Hynix was down about 4.0% and Samsung about 3.2% at 13:05 Seoul time, in Korea's first session since Thursday. The 5.0% and 4.0% falls shown below are too large.

Chip and AI stocks fell on Thursday after the Financial Times reported that OpenAI's annualised revenue was about $50 billion at the end of September, not the $68 billion widely reported late last month.
